BIO_ctrl_pending returns usize. `n <= 0` is not dead as a guard: it guards the empty-BIO `return None` path. The `< 0` half is unrepresentable for usize, so the guard's actual condition is `n == 0`. Changed to `n == 0`; semantically identical for usize.

EVP_PKEY_CTX_new_from_name had no SAFETY contract. Added the true one: c"DH" is NUL-terminated; a null library context selects the default; a null property query means none; the returned context is this frame's own allocation and is checked non-null immediately below.
The SAFETY text ('s is live') genuinely documents ossl_statem_in_error(s). It sat above assert_ne! with unsafe on the next line. Moved inside the macro argument, immediately above unsafe.

6424.what_was_wrong: A real missing contract, not a span artefact. The call has preconditions (NUL-terminated name; null default libctx and null propquery are deliberate) and returns a new owned context.
6424.repair: Three-line SAFETY comment stating exactly those preconditions and the frame ownership checked by the following assert!.

6324.what_was_wrong: A real bound expressed wrongly for an unsigned type, not dead code. The guard is the empty-write-BIO case; the `< 0` arm can never occur because BIO_ctrl_pending returns usize.

eight_macro_reports.diagnosis: All eight were the same Clippy lookback limitation: the SAFETY comment was placed above the macro name while the unsafe block began on the next line. The text was accurate for the operation in every case.
eight_macro_reports.empirical_control: A minimal crate with #![deny(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks)] reproduced the failure for `// SAFETY:` above a multi-line assert_eq! and passed when the same comment was placed immediately above the unsafe token. The probe was run in the court container and removed from the tree.
eight_macro_reports.chosen_repair: Move the comment, not add an allow. Moving satisfies Clippy's actual rule (line adjacency), removes the diagnostic rather than suppressing it, and avoids weakening the lint at any scope. No #[allow] was added anywhere in this subphase.

module_rationale_decision.reconstruction: No committed V1 artifact enumerates '22' directly. The committed V1 receipt records exactly 22 test_only blockers across the five modules that carry a module-level #[allow(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks)]: cipher_gcm 12 (10 blocks + 2 unsafe fn defs), obj 9 (5 blocks + 4 unsafe fn defs), thread 1 (one unsafe fn def). The seven allocator_seam blockers are all in secure.rs. That exact sum is the set decided here; it is not asserted independently of the V1 artifact.

module_rationale_decision.why_the_module_rationale_covers_the_rest: The five module rationales say that every test-side block is a direct call to the API under test with pointers to values the test owns. That is true of the remaining direct-call sites: the arguments are test-owned arrays/Vecs, static C literals, or literals/null whose validity the rationale states. No per-operation text was invented for them.
module_rationale_decision.not_claimed: This is not a claim that the five modules are discharged. After the additions, Clippy --force-warn still cannot associate 19 sites in those modules (obj 14, thread 5; secure 0, cipher_gcm 0, store_lib 0). Source inspection shows all 19 are the same macro-position pattern (SAFETY immediately above the macro name, unsafe on the following line), i.e. false positives rather than missing rationale. The pre-existing module-level allows remain in place; none was added, removed or weakened in this subphase.
